    Covariate-adjusted odds ratio

    Source: R/obs-adjusted.R
    epi_adjusted_odds_ratio.Rd

    Fits a binomial logistic regression with a binary exposure and selected covariates using maximum likelihood, reporting the exponentiated exposure coefficient with a normal-Wald confidence interval. Categorical covariates must be factors or logicals; continuous covariates enter linearly unless listed in nonlinear, in which case they enter as natural cubic splines with three degrees of freedom. This is a conditional odds ratio, not a risk ratio, and can differ from a marginal odds ratio even without confounding. It is not automatically a causal effect.

    Usage

    epi_adjusted_odds_ratio(
  .data,
  exposure,
  outcome,
  adjust = c(),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  weights = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  robust = c("model", "HC0", "HC1"),
  modifier = NULL,
  nonlinear = c()
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per individual.

    exposure

    Binary exposure column, coded 0/1.

    outcome

    Binary outcome column, coded 0/1.

    adjust

    Tidy selection of covariate columns, such as c(age, sex); defaults to none. Each must be numeric, factor, or logical and complete.

    conf_level

    Confidence level strictly between zero and one.

    weights

    Optional column of finite, non-negative observation weights.

    cluster

    Optional complete cluster identifier column. Observations within a cluster may be dependent; distinct clusters are assumed independent.

    robust

    Standard-error type: "model", "HC0" or "HC1".

    modifier

    Optional effect-modifier column with 2 to 10 levels; every level must contain both exposure groups.

    nonlinear

    Tidy selection of numeric adjust columns to model with natural splines (3 degrees of freedom) instead of linearly.

    Value

    An epi_result tibble with the exposure odds ratio, confidence limits, sample size, standard-error type and adjusted covariate names. With modifier, one row per modifier level plus interaction_p_value.

    Details

    Standard errors are model-based by default. robust = "HC0" or "HC1" requests sandwich standard errors (HC1 adds the n / (n - p) small-sample factor); supplying cluster sums scores within clusters and implies a sandwich estimator. Sandwich errors are recommended with weights, which are treated as sampling or analytic weights rather than frequency counts.

    With modifier, the model includes an exposure-by-modifier interaction and one row is returned per modifier level, giving the exposure effect within that level, together with a joint Wald p-value for the interaction terms.

    Complete data, independent observations (or independent clusters), a correctly specified model, adequate overlap and no serious separation are required; sparse data can render estimates and Wald intervals unreliable. Missing data are not handled.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(
  e = rep(0:1, each = 20), y = rep(c(0, 1, 0, 0, 1), 8),
  age = rep(20:29, 4), sex = rep(c("f", "m"), 20)
)
epi_adjusted_odds_ratio(d, e, y, adjust = age)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   measure             estimate conf_low conf_high     n se_type adjusted_for
#>   <chr>                  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <int> <chr>   <chr>       
#> 1 adjusted_odds_ratio        1    0.279      3.59    40 model   age         
epi_adjusted_odds_ratio(d, e, y, adjust = age, robust = "HC1")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   measure             estimate conf_low conf_high     n se_type adjusted_for
#>   <chr>                  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <int> <chr>   <chr>       
#> 1 adjusted_odds_ratio        1    0.265      3.78    40 HC1     age         
epi_adjusted_odds_ratio(d, e, y, adjust = age, modifier = sex)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>   measure             modifier modifier_level estimate conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>               <chr>    <chr>             <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 adjusted_odds_ratio sex      f                     1    0.164      6.10
#> 2 adjusted_odds_ratio sex      m                     1    0.164      6.10
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: interaction_p_value <dbl>, n <int>, se_type <chr>,
#> #   adjusted_for <chr>
